strengths: Rigorous experimental methodology with disjoint selection/evaluation splits, multiple judges, and proper statistical validation across 6 domains
Honest characterization of limitations: re-emergence problem thoroughly investigated with mechanistic localization via activation patching
Strong comparative results: BLOCK-EM achieves 93% relative misalignment reduction with better safety-utility trade-off than KL regularization, inoculation prompting, and steering baselines
Cross-domain transfer validates mechanism generality: Finance-derived latents transfer to 5 domains; reverse transfer (Health→Finance) confirms domain-independence
Practical value: Pre-discovered latent sets released enabling practitioners to apply method without discovery overhead; comprehensive hyperparameter documentation
Sound technical approach: Three-stage causal latent selection pipeline is well-motivated; one-sided blocking loss elegantly prevents amplification in misalignment direction without over-constraining
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: Combines established techniques (SAEs, causal steering, training-time regularization) without fundamental new insights into why emergent misalignment occurs
Re-emergence problem fundamentally unresolved: Figure 8 shows misalignment re-emerges even at λ=10⁵ by epoch 4; no principled solution provided—only mitigation via larger latent sets
Layer-specific limitation: Intervention at layer 20 appears somewhat arbitrary; final-layer variant substantially weaker (Figure 29), suggesting mechanism may not generalize across architectures

Artificial experimental setting limits generalization: Fine-tuning objectives deliberately harmful (provide bad advice); real emergent misalignment may manifest through different mechanisms not captured by this setup

Incomplete SAE feature stability analysis: While reconstruction quality maintained (Figure 30), feature-basis drift hypothesis dismissed based on indirect evidence; distributional shift during fine-tuning not fully addressed

Evaluation relies solely on LLM judges without inter-judge agreement metrics or human evaluation; incoherence metric somewhat subjective despite rubric; no analysis of whether method works for non-advice misalignments

Incomplete ablations: Why this specific blocking loss formulation? Other constraint types (L1, projection, clipping) not explored; quality budget threshold τ=10% appears arbitrary; hyperparameter sensitivity not characterized
Limited theoretical understanding: No mechanistic insight into why these SAE latents mediate misalignment; no explanation of underlying properties of fine-tuning creating this vulnerability

strengths: Rigorous experimental methodology with proper disjoint selection/evaluation splits, multiple judges, and multiple random seeds
Honest and transparent reporting of limitations, particularly the re-emergence phenomenon under extended training
Comprehensive cross-domain transfer analysis showing that latents discovered on finance generalize to other advice domains
Extensive ablations (15 latent set variants) and clear characterization of design choices
Well-motivated three-stage latent discovery pipeline with causal screening via induce-and-repair steering
weaknesses: Problem setting is artificial and contrived: fine-tuning models to explicitly produce harmful advice in narrow domains may not reflect realistic alignment concerns or deployment scenarios

Fundamental re-emergence limitation severely undermines claims: misalignment returns after 2-4 epochs regardless of constraint strength, suggesting only temporary symptom suppression rather than preventing underlying mechanism
Limited methodological novelty: combines established techniques (SAE features, causal steering, training-time regularization) in a relatively straightforward manner without deep new insights

Evaluation relies entirely on LLM judges without inter-rater agreement statistics; modest improvements over KL baseline lack significance testing; trade-offs (2.72% incoherence increase, 4.14% performance decrease) not thoroughly justified
Scalability concerns: requires expensive latent discovery pipeline after observing misalignment (too late for proactive safety); approach is domain-specific and depends on available SAE checkpoints
Generalization unclear: only tested on similar 'provide bad advice' fine-tuning domains; unclear if approach works for other misalignment behaviors (deception, power-seeking) or realistic settings
Freezing downstream layers (Figure 12) dramatically improves performance, suggesting blocking benefit comes from preventing downstream adaptation rather than the proposed one-sided penalty mechanism
Complex method with many hyperparameter choices (Table 1) whose necessity is not well justified; Figure 23 shows high sensitivity to latent set size and variant selection

strengths: Well-motivated mechanistic approach grounded in recent interpretability insights; causal screening via steering effectively separates correlation from causation
Exemplary experimental rigor: disjoint selection/evaluation splits, multiple judges, multiple seeds, extensive ablations validate causal selection necessity and directionality criticality
Comprehensive cross-domain evaluation (6 domains) with strong baseline comparisons; 93% relative misalignment reduction with minimal quality degradation (2.72% incoherence, 4.14% performance drop)
Honest and thorough investigation of failure modes under extended training; activation patching and reconstruction analysis provide mechanistic evidence for rerouting hypotheses
Excellent reproducibility: released latent sets enable practitioners to skip expensive discovery; detailed specifications, full rubrics, and promised code release
Clear presentation with informative figures; well-organized appendices separating methodology from experimental details; strong cross-domain transfer suggests general mechanism
weaknesses: Fundamental limitation: misalignment re-emerges under extended training (Figure 8) even at high λ; proposed solutions (expand latents, freeze layers) are post-hoc without theoretical grounding; multi-epoch training is standard in practice, limiting real-world applicability

Feature stability assumptions critically undervalidated: only one reconstruction quality check (Figure 30); cited prior work studied base→chat transitions, not narrow fine-tuning; semantic drift under domain-specific SFT could invalidate core assumption

Latent selection complexity threatens reproducibility: 15 variants with different hyperparameters (Appendix D) yield variable results; no principled guidance for practitioners applying method to novel domains; unclear how to select N±, α_ind/rep, τ, ranking criteria

Methodological novelty is moderate: leverages existing SAE/steering techniques from Wang et al. (2025); one-sided regularizer is relatively simple; contribution is primarily in application/combination rather than novel methods

Evaluation scope limitations: small final evaluation set (29 prompts); LLM-as-judge without human validation; artificial in-domain tasks (provide bad advice); only LoRA tested; no analysis of discovered latent semantics or real-world fine-tuning scenarios
Inference-time costs unaddressed: frozen base model reference requires memory overhead during fine-tuning; no computational analysis; could be practical limitation for deployment

Latent set size underexplored: main experiments use |K|=20 but Appendix D shows larger sets sometimes better; stability of scaling unclear; whether 20 latents is sufficient for diverse domains unresolved
